english.html: his bed — he thinking, nevertheless, that he had to do with his wife <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>; and yet St Augustine, although he excuses the incest, holds him guilty nonetheless of having let himself be vanquished and overcome by wine <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>. The last reason: that although there was no fraud, deceit or evil intention on the part of the said de Rols, the act is nevertheless so prodigious and evil, and the adultery of such pernicious example, that it ought to be punished in her <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. Which is nothing new in our law — namely, that a person without fault be punished if there is some great cause or public reason which commands it <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. Of which the example is at hand, of a curé, rector or prelate, if he becomes a leper: for because of the danger, scandal and abomination of the people, he will indeed be deprived of the administration of the benefice and of the Church <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>. And if someone has married a widow, or indeed a virgin who afterwards has fornicated, he is grievously wronged, so far is he from being at fault; and nevertheless this fault and lechery of his wife punishes him, and hinders him from being promoted to holy orders or admitted to any ecclesiastical ministry <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>. But on the contrary, for the excuse of the said de Rols, there comes first into consideration the weakness of her sex, easy to be deceived by the cunning, craftiness and sharp practice of men <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>, and in which the law does not readily presume fraud or any intention of doing wrong <sup class="mk" data-key="n">n</sup>. In the second place, the error in which she was justly placed, by reason of the great likeness there was between the said du Tilh and Martin Guerre, accompanied by innumerable tokens which this du Tilh had given her, of the most private, together with the sisters and uncle of the said Martin — nay, to all those of the place of Artigat who presented themselves to him, and who on this account had all received him as Martin Guerre — ought to excuse the said de Rols, after the example of Lot <sup class="mk" data-key="o">o</sup>, of whom we have spoken, and more properly still of Abimelech, King of Gerar, who had taken possession of Sarah, Abraham's wife, and wished to abuse her, thinking she was Abraham's sister, as he had assured him; nevertheless he was excused and pardoned by God, because Abimelech had undertaken this deed by error and, as the Scripture speaks, in the simplicity of his heart and the purity of his hands <sup class="mk" data-key="p">p</sup>. And indeed in a like

notes.gloss: Lot and his daughters. As at annot-010 {i}, Coras's "thinking he had to do with his wife" is his gloss; the text says Lot did not perceive it.

notes.citation: Augustine, Contra Faustum (the print says book 1; the discussion of Lot is in book 22, chs. 43–44); Decretum, C. 15 q. 1, c. Inebriaverunt (chapter not verified)
notes.original: S. Aguſtin au liure i. contra Fauſtum c. inebriauerunt. xv. q. i.
notes.gloss: Augustine excuses Lot of the incest, which he did not know, and blames the drunkenness that made it possible. C. 15 q. 1 is the quaestio on offences committed in drunkenness; cited again at {o} and {r}.

notes.citation: Digest 48.19 (De poenis), l. Si quis aliquid (D. 48.19.38, Paulus), § Qui abortionis (§ 5)
notes.original: l. ſi quis aliquid. P. q abortionis. D. de pœn.
notes.gloss: Those who give abortifacients or love-potions, even without evil intent, are punished quia mali exempli res est — because the thing is of bad example: Coras's "a person without fault … punished" for the example.

notes.original: c. ſine culpa. de reg. iu. au vi.
notes.gloss: Sine culpa, nisi subsit causa, non est aliquis puniendus — without fault no one is to be punished, unless there is a cause. Cited again at {p}.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 3.6 (De clerico aegrotante vel debilitato), c. Tua nos (chapter not verified)
notes.gloss: The leprous cleric is relieved of the administration of his church, a coadjutor being given him.

notes.citation: Decretum, D. 34, cc. Si quis viduam and Si cuius (chapter numbers not verified; the first is Apostolic canon 18, the second canon 8 of Neocaesarea)
notes.original: c. ſi cuius. v. ſi quis viduã xxxiiij. diſt.
notes.gloss: He who has married a widow or a woman put away, or whose wife has committed adultery, may not be admitted to or remain in orders. The v. between the two incipits is read as & c.; the transcribers' xxxiij. would put the canons in D. 33, where they are not.

notes.citation: Digest 48.5 (Ad legem Iuliam de adulteriis coercendis), l. Si adulterium (D. 48.5.39(38), Papinian), § 1 (paragraph's bearing not verified); Novel 97 (De aequalitate dotis et propter nuptias donationis, Authenticum coll. 7), § Quaesitum (paragraph not verified)
notes.original: l. ſi adulteriũ. P. i. D. de adul. P. quæſitũ. de æqualita. dot. Aux nouuelles collation vij.
notes.gloss: Both cited for the weakness of the female sex, which the law favours; the Novel was cited the same way at annot-075 {c}.

notes.citation: Code 9.8 (Ad legem Iuliam maiestatis), l. Quisquis (C. 9.8.5, Arcadius and Honorius), § Ad filias (§ 3)
notes.original: l. quiſquis. P. ad filias. C. ad l. Iul. maieſta.
notes.gloss: The daughters of a traitor are treated more mildly than his sons, quia infirmitate sexus minus ausuras esse confidimus — because by the weakness of their sex we trust they will dare less.

notes.citation: Genesis 19; Decretum, C. 15 q. 1, c. Inebriaverunt, as at {g}
notes.original: Geneſ. xix. c. inebriauerunt. xv. q. i.

notes.citation: Genesis 20 (20:1–7; "in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands", v. 5); Decretum, C. 32 q. 4, c. Nemo (chapter not verified)
notes.original: Gene. c. xx. c. nemo. xxxij. q. iiij.
notes.gloss: Abimelech, king of Gerar, takes Sarah, whom Abraham has called his sister, and is warned by God in a dream before he touches her. Coras's "wished to abuse her" and "pardoned by God" follow the story; the Genesis 26 Abimelech of annot-082 {r} is the later king and Isaac's wife.

& neantmoins S. Auguſtin, bien que l'excuſe de l'in-
ceſte le rend toutesſois coulpable de ce qu'il ſ'eſtoit
laiſſé viancre & ſurmõter au vin {g}. La derniere raiſon, q̃
iaçoit n'y euſt dol, fraude, ni mauuaiſe intention de la
part de ladite de Rols: l'acte pourtãt eſt ſi prodigieux,
& mauuais, & l'adultere de ſi pernicieux exemple, qu'il
deuroit eſtre puni en elle {h}. Ce que n'eſt nouueau en
noſtre droict, à ſçauoir qu'vn perſonnage ſans coulpe
ſoit puni, ſ'il y a quelque grande cauſe ou raiſon publi-
que qui le commande {i}. Dequoy l'exemple eſt preſent,
d'vn curé, recteur, ou prelat, ſ'il deuient ladre: car pour
le danger, ſcandalle, & abomination du peuple, on luy.
oſtera bien l'adminiſtration du benefice, & de l'Egliſe {k}
Et ſi quelqu'vn a eſpouſé vne vefue, ou biẽ vne vierge,
laquelle apres a paillardé, il eſt griefuement offenſé, tãt
ſ'en fault qu'il ſoit en coulpe: & neantmoins ceſte faute

promeu aux ordres ſacrez, ou admis à aucun miniſtere
eccleſiaſtique {l}. Mais au contraire, pour l'excuſe de la-
dite de Rols, vient premierement en conſideration, la
foibleſſe de ſon ſexe, facile à eſtre deceu, par l'aſtuce, cal

ment ne preſume point dol, ou intẽtiõ aucune de mal
faire {n}. En ſecond lieu, l'erreur auquel elle eſtoit iuſte-
ment poſee, pour la grande ſimilitude qui eſtoit entre
leſdits du Tilh, & Martin Guerre, accompagnee d'in
nombrables enſeignes, qu'iceluy du Tilh luy auoit dõ-

Martin: voire à tous ceux du lieu d'Artigat qui ſe pre-
ſentoient à luy, & leſquels à ceſte occaſion l'auoyent
tous receu pour Martin Guerre: deuoit excuſer ladite
de Rols, à l'exẽple de Loth {o}, duquel a eſté parlé, & plus

readings.reason: luy, the pronoun (du Tilh luy auoit donnees); lüy with a diaeresis is not a form this print uses.
The canons Si quis viduam and Si cuius (uxor adulterium commiserit) stand in Gratian's Distinctio 34, on the marriages of clerics; xxxiiij. is right and xxxiij. would misplace them.
col-|lation is the word collation divided across two margin lines; the hyphen is the expected sign of division. Same citation either way.
